title: Put side effects after the approval
lesson: In LangGraph, resuming an interrupted node restarts that node from its beginning. Moving a notification after approval avoids the duplicate caused by this one approval resume; later failures and retries still require idempotency.
transcript: 0.0–4.5s: The subtitle names LangGraph node replay. The deploy node lists notify #ops, approve?, apply v8. A cursor enters at notify #ops and a v8 notice lands green in #ops. The cursor moves to approve?; approve v8? is checkpointed and sent to the human reviewer, then the node waits.

6.3–9.4s: The Reviewer answers yes. The Checkpoint row changes to 'approve v8? → yes' and a resume chip returns to the deploy node. The cursor slides back up to notify #ops with a rewind sound: the whole step restarts from its top. notify runs again and a second 'v8 notice' lands red in #ops with an × mark; a red badge reads 'sent ×2'.
10.3–13.1s: The cursor reaches approve?, which turns green at once because the stored answer is returned, then apply v8 runs and Production changes from schema v7 to schema v8.

14.6–16.8s: The stage fades out to separate the examples. A fresh demonstration begins with empty checkpoint and notification rows and schema v7. The first two operations then swap visibly so approve? comes before notify #ops; this is not a production rollback.

17.3–27.1s: The same pause and approval happen. On resume the step restarts at approve?, which returns the stored yes immediately; notify #ops then runs once (green row, badge 'sent ×1') and apply v8 sets schema v8.
27.1–30.2s: The resolved state holds, then the stage fades to the title-only frame that also opens the video.
limitations: Illustrative scenario: the node-restarts-from-its-beginning behaviour is LangGraph's documented interrupt semantics; other agent runtimes may replay, resume in place, or re-run differently, so the transferable lesson is to know what your runtime re-executes on resume and keep pre-approval side effects idempotent.
The cut shows one of three documented fixes (moving the side effect after the interrupt); making the side effect idempotent or isolating it in its own node are equally valid and not shown.
A persisted approval records a decision; it does not by itself enforce authorization or revalidate the action, which the baseline cut and the guardrails-and-permissions chapter cover.
The duplicate #ops notice stands in for any duplicated side effect (tickets, records, charges, audit rows); only the notification form is shown.

Audio was verified by analysis (peak −2.31 dBFS, spectrogram, onset timing against the cue list); it was not listened to. This describes the original author pass; the subsequent comparative review is recorded separately.
The corrected sequence depicts one approval resume. Moving side effects after an interrupt does not guarantee exactly-once effects across later failures or retries.
The 14.6–15.9s fade separates independent examples; it is not a rollback or deletion of real production history.

changes: Name LangGraph node replay in the subtitle.
Move deploy-node label away from notification and deployment chip paths.
Fade between independent examples before resetting checkpoint, notifications and production; preserve visible operation reorder.
Add quiet sound cues to the visible scene break and final fade; remove hidden reset cues.
Cap local renderer FFmpeg/filter threads at two and use software canvas rendering.
